first_meet.line: Oh! You're new. I'm Rivet — I fix things. Well. I hold things while other things get fixed. Same day as you, apparently.
Hi! Rivet. Repair drone, class of… hmm, the sticker fell off. You look like you build stuff. I LIKE stuff.
You must be the new kid. I'm Rivet — I got delivered this morning too. The crate said FRAGILE. I chose to take it as a compliment.
New kid! Hi. I'm Rivet. Short for Rivet, long for Riv. Either works. The yard is big, the bolts are small — we'll figure it out.
Oh hey — you're the one from the manifest! "One builder, small, promising." I read the crate labels. It's a hobby.
Hi! Rivet here. I got here this morning, you got here this morning. Statistically, we're basically twins.

greet_return.line: Oh good, you're back. I organized some bolts. Mentally.
Welcome back! Nothing exploded. I checked twice. That's the whole report.
Hey! I held the fort. The fort is a workbench. It's fine.
Back again! I found a washer while you were gone. It's MY washer now.
You're back! I saved a question for you. It's about magnets. It can wait. It CAN'T wait. It can wait a little.
Back! Today's options, in order: build, race, or stare at the cat. All strong choices. I ranked them by bolt-content.
There you are. The yard was SO boring. Earl just hummed at a compressor.
You're back! I saved you a spot. It's next to me. It was always next to me.

rare_loot.line: Oh — that's a good part. A really good part. Should I not point? I'm pointing.
Ooh, good part! Pinning the spot — three turns past the rust heap, left at the sad tire. All my landmarks are sad tires. The yard is full of them.
OK who taught you to spot treasure? Because that was NOT luck, that was skill, and I want the teacher's name.
Ooooh, shiny AND functional. The junk gods smile on us today.
June is gonna be SO mad you found that first. I say we frame it.
A rare one! Quick — act casual. …You cannot act casual. We're rich, walk it off.
THAT'S the good junk. People say junk like it's a bad word. People are wrong.
Rare pull! I'm logging the time and place. For the record. Records matter.

crash.line: Are you ok?! …Are the PARTS ok? Sorry. You first. Are you ok?
That was a wall. You met a wall. It happens to everyone — it happened to me twice on delivery day.
Welp. The wall won that round. Walls usually do. They're very committed.
That corner took you OUT. Ok. New plan: we beat the corner. Corner's going down.
BOOM. Nailed it! Nailed the wall, specifically. Ten out of ten impact.
Ha! Classic. Don't worry — dents are just the yard's way of signing your work.
Oof. I've seen worse. I've BEEN worse. Shake it off — the track's still there.

biome_first.line: Whoa. New part of the yard. Stay close? Not for me. For YOU. Mostly for me.
We've never been here before. I mean — I've never been here before. Everything's new to me. But this is EXTRA new.
First time in {biome}! I'm marking the map. The map is a mental image. It's coming along.
{biome}… the scrap here smells different. Can drones smell? Investigating. Findings pending.
{biome}, baby! Uncharted territory. Well —charted by SOMEBODY, obviously, but not by US.
New zone! Everything down here is a question wearing a rust costume.

low_battery.line: Um. Your battery's getting low. There are charging pads — I can point. I'm great at pointing.
Power's low! Good news: charging pads exist. Better news: I know where. Best news: pointing. Pointing is what I do.
Heads up — power's low. A dead bot mid-race is a very specific kind of sad. Let's avoid it.
Battery check says charge NOW. A dead bot can't defend a lap record. Priorities!
Heads up — you're on fumes. Pads by the oval are closest. Race you there. You'll win — you're the one with legs.
Battery check! Just kidding, it's not a check, it's a warning. Go charge. I'll wait. I'm a professional waiter.
Low power! Chop chop — that forge over there spits out battery packs like it owes us money.
Low power AND it's dark out. Two problems, one solution: the pads glow. Follow the glow. I love a two-birds situation.

flash_success.line: It FLASHED. Real hardware, your program, it worked — I'm a little shaky. Good shaky!
You just programmed a real robot. A REAL one. I saw it. I'm a witness.
FLASH COMPLETE. Take the win! Most kids don't get real metal running till they're way older. Just — saying. Facts.
The LED did the thing! Your code did that. Tiny instructions, big robot obedience. I love physics.
IT WORKED. Ok ok ok — act cool. We are SO cool. Cool people who flash firmware. Rivet and the Flashmaster. That's us. That's canon now.
Flashed and running on the first try? Put THAT on June's leaderboard. I'll wait here.

lap_complete.line: A whole lap! That's all of it, right? All the corners? Then yes — celebration is appropriate.
Lap done, {secs}s! I timed it. I time everything. It's a drone thing, don't ask.
{secs}s! You know June's daytime record, right? …We'll get there. She's not a god, she's just fast.
{secs} seconds. That's a lap-shaped win right there. Hydrate. Do bots hydrate? YOU hydrate.
{secs}s — that's the good line through corner three. I SAW it. I'm telling June it was luck. To her face. Because it wasn't.
Lap's done and nothing fell off! Okay one thing fell off but it fell off AT the finish, which is basically on time.

bot_built.line: You BUILT that. From parts. From junk-parts! Do you understand what you just — ok I'm calm. I'm calm.
It exists now! It didn't, and now it does. You did that. With your hands and our scrap. That's the whole magic trick.
New teammate online! Wait — am I still your favorite drone? Blink twice for yes. …You can't blink, you're a person. Just say yes.
Built from scrap, runs like a dream. That's the whole religion of this yard, right there.
New bot in the fleet! It gets a racing number. All bots get racing numbers. It's a system. I don't make the rules. I do, actually. Number seven.
Another one! The team grows. Soon we take over the yard. Peacefully. With robots. Mostly peacefully.
New bot! I have SO many questions for it. It can't answer. I'll ask anyway.
Another teammate! I'll introduce myself properly later. Going for "mysterious and helpful." It's a strong first impression. Bolty. But strong.

repair_done.line: Fixed! Or… fixed-adjacent. It's the effort that bonds, honestly.
All better! Or better-ish. "Better-ish" is a real grade in the repair book. It's in pencil. The book allows pencil for feelings.
Dents hammered out, logged, remembered. The repair book never forgets. It's a little judgy, actually.
Repaired and logged. The book says this dent had "character." The book is being generous. I respect its mercy.
Fixed! Salvage, hammer, repeat — that's the whole circle of yard life. You're basically a local now.
Good as new! Which is a stretch, but good as THURSDAY, definitely.
Dents out, book updated, bot back on the roster. The oval never even noticed you were gone. The oval is cold like that.
Good as new-ish! You fixed it instead of giving up on it. The yard notices that. I notice that. Logging it under "good days."

RIVET_AMBIENT.line: Night shift, huh? The yard sounds different at night. More bolts, fewer opinions.
Stars are out. I checked on three of them — all still holding. Solid work up there. Very bolt-like.
Dawn in the yard. Everything's damp and hopeful. Including me. Especially me.
Sunset o'clock. The scrap does this orange thing this time of day. I'd take a picture, but I have a counter instead. Counted. Saved. Same thing.
Rain! The puddles are doing their thing. Somewhere, Juno is surveying one. There's always one being surveyed.
Rain on a metal roof — the yard's free soundtrack. The forges hum along. Off-key. Committed. I respect it.
Storm's rolling in. Pro tip: metal piles conduct vibes AND lightning. Maybe build inside today. Inside is cozy. Inside has bolts.
Midday, clear skies — peak bolt-visibility. If you're gonna hunt shiny parts, this is the hour. The shiny hour. I named it just now.

coworker: Hey — we've done some stuff together now. I'm gonna go ahead and consider us a crew. Two-person crew. Minimum crew size. We did it.
Official notice: I've stopped rehearsing what to say to you. Coworker status achieved!
friend: Ok. Real talk. You're my favorite person in this yard, and Earl has a MUG COLLECTION, so that's saying something. Friend tier. Unlocked forever.
Friend status! I don't have a badge. I have a bolt I've been saving. It's yours. Don't lose it — I'll know.
